shloka_text: कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य युधाजित्केकयो नृपः । स्वगुरुं प्रेषयामास राघवाय महात्मने । गार्ग्यमङ्गिरसः पुत्रं ब्रह्मर्षिममितप्रभम् ।। 7.100.1 ।।
transliteration: kasyacittvatha kālasya yudhājitkekayo nṛpaḥ | svaguruṃ preṣayāmāsa rāghavāya mahātmane | gārgyamaṅgirasaḥ putraṃ brahmarṣimamitaprabham || 7.100.1 ||
translation: कस्यचित् some, त्वथ then, कालस्य of time, युधाजित् Yudhājit, केकयो Kekaya, नृपः king, स्वगुरुम् his own preceptor, प्रेषयामास sent, राघवाय to Rama, महात्मने to the great-souled one, गार्ग्यम् Gārgya, अङ्गिरसः of Angiras, पुत्रम् son, ब्रह्मर्षिम् a Brahmarshi, अमितप्रभम् of immeasurable splendor.
explanation: Then, after some time, King Yudhājit of Kekaya sent his own preceptor, Gārgya, the son of Angiras, a Brahmarshi of immeasurable splendor, to the great-souled Rama.
comments: King Yudhajit of Kekaya sends his preceptor Gargya with rich gifts, proposing that Rama conquer the beautiful Gandharva land on the banks of the Sindhu, held by three crore Gandharvas, sons of Shailusha -- Rama agrees and sends Bharata with his sons Taksha and Pushkala and an army to subdue them and found two cities, and the host, followed by flesh-eating creatures, marches to Kekaya.

shloka_text: दश चाश्वसहस्राणि प्रीतिदानमनुत्तमम् ।। 7.100.2 ।।
transliteration: daśa cāśvasahasrāṇi prītidānamanuttamam || 7.100.2 ||
translation: दश ten, च and, अश्वसहस्राणि thousands of horses, प्रीतिदानम् a gift of affection, अनुत्तमम् unsurpassed.
explanation: And ten thousand horses, an unsurpassed gift of affection, were also sent.

shloka_text: कम्बलानि च रत्नानि चित्रवस्त्रमथोत्तमम् । रामाय प्रददौ राजा शुभान्याभरणानि च ।। 7.100.3 ।।
transliteration: kambalāni ca ratnāni citravastramathottamam | rāmāya pradadau rājā śubhānyābharaṇāni ca || 7.100.3 ||
translation: कम्बलानि blankets, च and, रत्नानि jewels, चित्रवस्त्रम् colorful garments, अथ then, उत्तमम् excellent, रामाय to Rama, प्रददौ gave, राजा the king, शुभानि auspicious, आभरणानि ornaments, च and.
explanation: The king also gave blankets, jewels, excellent colorful garments, and auspicious ornaments to Rama.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा तु राघवो धीमान्महर्षिं गार्ग्यमागतम् । मातुलस्याश्वपतिनः प्रहितं तन्महाधनम् ।। 7.100.4 ।।
transliteration: śrutvā tu rāghavo dhīmānmaharṣiṃ gārgyamāgatam | mātulasyāśvapatinaḥ prahitaṃ tanmahādhanam || 7.100.4 ||
translation: श्रुत्वा having heard, तु and, राघवः Rama, धीमान् the intelligent, महर्षिम् the great sage, गार्ग्यम् Gargya, आगतम् who had arrived, मातुलस्य of the maternal uncle, अश्वपतिनः Ashvapati, प्रहितम् sent, तत् that, महाधनम् great wealth.
explanation: The intelligent Rama, having heard that the great sage Gargya, sent by his maternal uncle Ashvapati with great wealth, had arrived.

shloka_text: प्रत्युद्गम्य च काकुत्स्थः क्रोशमात्रं सहानुजः । गार्ग्यं सम्पूजयामास यथा शक्रो बृहस्पतिम् ।। 7.100.5 ।।
transliteration: pratyudgamya ca kākutsthaḥ krośamātraṃ sahānujaḥ | gārgyaṃ sampūjayāmāsa yathā śakro bṛhaspatim || 7.100.5 ||
translation: प्रत्युद्गम्य having gone forth to meet, च and, काकुत्स्थः Rama, क्रोशमात्रम् for a distance of a krosa, सहानुजः with his younger brothers, गार्ग्यम् Gargya, सम्पूजयामास honored greatly, यथा just as, शक्रः Indra, बृहस्पतिम् Brihaspati.
explanation: And Rama, along with his younger brothers, went forth for a krosa to meet Gargya and honored him greatly, just as Indra honors Brihaspati.

shloka_text: तथा सम्पूज्य तमृषिं तद्धनं प्रतिगृह्य च । पृष्ट्वा प्रतिपदं सर्वं कुशलं मातुलस्य च । उपविष्टं महाभागं रामः प्रष्टुं प्रचक्रमे ।। 7.100.6 ।।
transliteration: tathā sampūjya tamṛṣiṃ taddhanaṃ pratigṛhya ca | pṛṣṭvā pratipadaṃ sarvaṃ kuśalaṃ mātulasya ca | upaviṣṭaṃ mahābhāgaṃ rāmaḥ praṣṭuṃ pracakrame || 7.100.6 ||
translation: तथा thus, सम्पूज्य having honored greatly, तम् that, ऋषिम् sage, तत् that, धनम् wealth, प्रतिगृह्य having received, च and, पृष्ट्वा having asked, प्रतिपदम् every detail, सर्वम् all, कुशलम् welfare, मातुलस्य of the maternal uncle, च and, उपविष्टम् seated, महाभागम् the highly fortunate one, रामः Rama, प्रष्टुम् to ask, प्रचक्रमे began.
explanation: Having thus greatly honored that sage, received the wealth, and inquired about every detail of his maternal uncle's welfare, Rama then began to question the highly fortunate sage who was now seated.

shloka_text: किमाह मातुलो वाक्यं यदर्थं भगवानिह । प्राप्तो वाक्यविदां श्रेष्ठः साक्षादिव बृहस्पतिः ।। 7.100.7 ।।
transliteration: kimāha mātulo vākyaṃ yadarthaṃ bhagavāniha | prāpto vākyavidāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ sākṣādiva bṛhaspatiḥ || 7.100.7 ||
translation: किम् what, आह said, मातुलः the maternal uncle, वाक्यम् message, यदर्थम् for which purpose, भगवान् the revered one, इह here, प्राप्तः arrived, वाक्यविदाम् among those skilled in speech, श्रेष्ठः the best, साक्षात् directly, इव as if, बृहस्पतिः Brihaspati.
explanation: Rama asked what message his maternal uncle had sent, for which purpose the revered sage, who is the best among those skilled in speech, had arrived here, as if Brihaspati himself.

shloka_text: रामस्य भाषितं श्रुत्वा महर्षिः कार्यविस्तरम् । वक्तुमद्भुतसङ्काशं राघवायोपचक्रमे ।। 7.100.8 ।।
transliteration: rāmasya bhāṣitaṃ śrutvā maharṣiḥ kāryavistaram | vaktumadbhutasaṅkāśaṃ rāghavāyopacakrame || 7.100.8 ||
translation: रामस्य Rama's, भाषितम् words, श्रुत्वा having heard, महर्षिः the great sage, कार्यविस्तरम् the detailed matter, वक्तुम् to tell, अद्भुतसङ्काशम् wonderful, राघवाय to Rama, उपचक्रमे began.
explanation: Having heard Rama's words, the great sage began to narrate the detailed and wonderful matter to Rama.

shloka_text: मातुलस्ते महाबाहो वाक्यमाह नरर्षभः । युधाजित्प्रीतिसंयुक्तं श्रूयतां यदि रोचते ।। 7.100.9 ।।
transliteration: mātulaste mahābāho vākyamāha nararṣabhaḥ | yudhājitprītisaṃyuktaṃ śrūyatāṃ yadi rocate || 7.100.9 ||
translation: मातुलः maternal uncle, ते your, महाबाहो O mighty-armed one, वाक्यम् words, आह said, नरर्षभः O best among men, युधाजित् Yudhājit, प्रीतिसंयुक्तम् filled with affection, श्रूयताम् let it be heard, यदि if, रोचते it pleases.
explanation: Yudhājit, your maternal uncle, O mighty-armed Rama, has spoken words filled with affection, which you should hear if they please you.

shloka_text: अयं गन्धर्वविषयः फलमूलोपशोभितः । सिन्धोरुभयतः पार्श्वे देशः परमशोभनः ।। 7.100.10 ।।
transliteration: ayaṃ gandharvaviṣayaḥ phalamūlopaśobhitaḥ | sindhorubhayataḥ pārśve deśaḥ paramaśobhanaḥ || 7.100.10 ||
translation: अयम् this, गन्धर्वविषयः region of Gandharvas, फलमूलोपशोभितः adorned with fruits and roots, सिन्धोः of the Sindhu (river), उभयतः on both sides, पार्श्वे on the banks, देशः region, परमशोभनः exceedingly beautiful.
explanation: This region of the Gandharvas, adorned with fruits and roots, lies on both banks of the Sindhu river and is exceedingly beautiful.

shloka_text: तं च रक्षन्ति गन्धर्वाः सायुधा युद्धकोविदाः । शैलूषस्य सुता वीर त्रिकोट्यो वै महाबलाः ।। 7.100.11 ।।
transliteration: taṃ ca rakṣanti gandharvāḥ sāyudhā yuddhakovidāḥ | śailūṣasya sutā vīra trikoṭyo vai mahābalāḥ || 7.100.11 ||
translation: तम् that, च and, रक्षन्ति protect, गन्धर्वाः Gandharvas, सायुधाः armed, युद्धकोविदाः skilled in warfare, शैलूषस्य of Shailūṣa, सुताः sons, वीर O hero, त्रिकोट्यः three crores, वै indeed, महाबलाः very powerful.
explanation: O hero, that region is protected by three crores of very powerful Gandharvas, the sons of Shailūṣa, who are armed and skilled in warfare.

shloka_text: तान्विनिर्जित्य काकुत्स्थ गन्धर्वनगरं शुभम् । निवेशय महाबोहो स्वे पुरे सुसमाहिते ।। 7.100.12 ।।
transliteration: tānvinirjitya kākutstha gandharvanagaraṃ śubham | niveśaya mahāboho sve pure susamāhite || 7.100.12 ||
translation: तान् them, विनिर्जित्य having conquered, काकुत्स्थ O descendant of Kakutstha, गन्धर्वनगरम् city of Gandharvas, शुभम् auspicious, निवेशय establish, महाबाहो O mighty-armed one, स्वे your own, पुरे city, सुसमाहिते well-established.
explanation: O mighty-armed Rama, descendant of Kakutstha, having conquered those Gandharvas, establish your own well-governed and auspicious city in that Gandharva region.

shloka_text: अन्यस्य न गतिस्तत्र देशः परमशोभनः । रोचतां ते महाबाहो नाहं त्वामहितं वदे ।। 7.100.13 ।।
transliteration: anyasya na gatistatra deśaḥ paramaśobhanaḥ | rocatāṃ te mahābāho nāhaṃ tvāmahitaṃ vade || 7.100.13 ||
translation: अन्यस्य for anyone else, न not, गतिः access, तत्र there, देशः region, परमशोभनः exceedingly beautiful, रोचताम् let it please, ते you, महाबाहो O mighty-armed one, न not, अहम् I, त्वाम् you, अहितम् harmful, वदे speak.
explanation: No one else has access to that exceedingly beautiful region; O mighty-armed one, may this proposal please you, for I would never speak anything harmful to you.

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा राघवः प्रीतो महर्षेर्मातुलस्य च । उवाच बाढमित्येव भरतं चान्ववैक्षत ।। 7.100.14 ।।
transliteration: tacchrutvā rāghavaḥ prīto maharṣermātulasya ca | uvāca bāḍhamityeva bharataṃ cānvavaikṣata || 7.100.14 ||
translation: तत् that (proposal), श्रुत्वा having heard, राघवः Rama, प्रीतः pleased, महर्षेः of the great sage (Valmiki), मातुलस्य of the maternal uncle (Yudhajit), च and, उवाच said, बाढम् certainly, इति एव thus, भरतम् Bharata, च and, अन्ववैक्षत looked at.
explanation: Hearing the proposal from the great sage and his maternal uncle, Rama, pleased, agreed and then looked at Bharata.

shloka_text: सो ऽब्रवीद्राघवः प्रीतः साञ्जलिप्रग्रहो द्विजम् । इमौ कुमारौ तं देशं ब्रह्मर्षे विचरिष्यतः ।। 7.100.15 ।।
transliteration: so 'bravīdrāghavaḥ prītaḥ sāñjalipragraho dvijam | imau kumārau taṃ deśaṃ brahmarṣe vicariṣyataḥ || 7.100.15 ||
translation: सः he, अब्रवीत् said, राघवः Rama, प्रीतः pleased, स-अञ्जलि-प्रग्रहः with folded hands, द्विजम् to the Brahmin (Valmiki), इमौ these two, कुमारौ princes, तम् that, देशम् region, ब्रह्मर्षे O Brahmarshi (Valmiki), विचरिष्यतः will go forth/will rule.
explanation: Pleased, Rama, with folded hands, said to the Brahmarshi Valmiki, "O Brahmarshi, these two princes will go forth to that region."

shloka_text: भरतस्यात्मजौ वीरौ तक्षः पुष्कल एव च । मातुलेन सुगुप्तौ तु धर्मेण सुसमाहितौ ।। 7.100.16 ।।
transliteration: bharatasyātmajau vīrau takṣaḥ puṣkala eva ca | mātulena suguptau tu dharmeṇa susamāhitau || 7.100.16 ||
translation: भरतस्य of Bharata, आत्मजौ sons, वीरौ valiant, तक्षः Taksha, पुष्कलः Pushkala, एव indeed, च and, मातुलेन by the maternal uncle (Yudhajit), सुगुप्तौ well-protected, तु indeed, धर्मेण with righteousness, सुसमाहितौ well-established/well-trained.
explanation: These are Bharata's valiant sons, Taksha and Pushkala, who are well-protected by their maternal uncle and well-trained in righteousness.

shloka_text: भरतं चाग्रतः कृत्वा कुमारौ सबलानुगौ । निहत्य गन्धर्वसुतान्द्वे पुरे विभजिष्यतः ।। 7.100.17 ।।
transliteration: bharataṃ cāgrataḥ kṛtvā kumārau sabalānugau | nihatya gandharvasutāndve pure vibhajiṣyataḥ || 7.100.17 ||
translation: भरतम् Bharata, च and, अग्रतः in front, कृत्वा having placed/making, कुमारौ the two princes, स-बल-अनुगौ accompanied by an army, निहत्य having killed, गन्धर्व-सुतान् the sons of Gandharvas, द्वे two, पुरे cities, विभजिष्यतः will divide.
explanation: With Bharata leading, the two princes, accompanied by an army, will kill the sons of the Gandharvas and then establish two cities.

shloka_text: निवेश्य ते पुरवरे आत्मजौ सन्निवेश्य च । आगमिष्यति मे भूयः सकाशमतिधार्मिकः ।। 7.100.18 ।।
transliteration: niveśya te puravare ātmajau sanniveśya ca | āgamiṣyati me bhūyaḥ sakāśamatidhārmikaḥ || 7.100.18 ||
translation: निवेश्य having established, ते those, पुरवरे excellent cities, आत्मजौ his sons, सन्निवेश्य having settled, च and, आगमिष्यति will return, मे to me, भूयः again, सकाशम् to the presence, अतिधार्मिकः the very righteous one (Bharata).
explanation: Having established those excellent cities and settled his sons there, the very righteous Bharata will return to my presence again.

shloka_text: ब्रह्मर्षिमेवमुक्त्वा तु भरतं सबलानुगम् । आज्ञापयामास तदा कुमारौ चाभ्यषेचयत् ।। 7.100.19 ।।
transliteration: brahmarṣimevamuktvā tu bharataṃ sabalānugam | ājñāpayāmāsa tadā kumārau cābhyaṣecayat || 7.100.19 ||
translation: ब्रह्मर्षिम् the Brahmarshi, एवम् thus, उक्त्वा having spoken to, तु indeed, भरतम् Bharata, सबलानुगम् with his army and followers, आज्ञापयामास commanded, तदा then, कुमारौ the two princes, च and, अभ्यषेचयत् consecrated.
explanation: Having thus spoken to the Brahmarshi Vashistha, Rama then commanded Bharata, who was accompanied by his army and followers, and consecrated the two princes.

shloka_text: नक्षत्रेण च सौम्येन पुरस्कृत्याङ्गिरस्सुतम् । भरतः सह सैन्येन कुमाराभ्यां विनिर्ययौ ।। 7.100.20 ।।
transliteration: nakṣatreṇa ca saumyena puraskṛtyāṅgirassutam | bharataḥ saha sainyena kumārābhyāṃ viniryayau || 7.100.20 ||
translation: नक्षत्रेण by the constellation, च and, सौम्येन auspicious, पुरस्कृत्य having placed in front (honoring), अङ्गिरस्सुतम् the son of Angiras (Vashistha), भरतः Bharata, सह with, सैन्येन the army, कुमाराभ्याम् with the two princes, विनिर्ययौ set out.
explanation: Bharata, honoring Vashistha (the son of Angiras) and choosing an auspicious constellation, set out with his army and the two princes.

shloka_text: सा सेना शक्रयुक्तेव नगरान्निर्ययावथ । राघवानुगता दूरं दुराधर्षा सुरैरपि ।। 7.100.21 ।।
transliteration: sā senā śakrayukteva nagarānniryayāvatha | rāghavānugatā dūraṃ durādharṣā surairapi || 7.100.21 ||
translation: सा that, सेना army, शक्रयुक्ता accompanied by Indra, इव as if, नगरान् from the city, निर्ययाव departed, अथ then, राघवानुगता following the Raghava (Bharata), दूरम् far, दुराधर्षा unconquerable, सुरैः by gods, अपि even.
explanation: That army, as if accompanied by Indra, then departed far from the city, following Bharata, and was unconquerable even by the gods.

shloka_text: मांसादानि च सत्त्वानि रक्षांसि सुमहान्ति च । अनुजग्मुर्हि भरतं रुधिरस्य पिपासया ।। 7.100.22 ।।
transliteration: māṃsādāni ca sattvāni rakṣāṃsi sumahānti ca | anujagmurhi bharataṃ rudhirasya pipāsayā || 7.100.22 ||
translation: मांसादानि flesh-eating, च and, सत्त्वानि beings, रक्षांसि Rakshasas, सुमहान्ति very great, च and, अनुजग्मुः followed, हि indeed, भरतम् Bharata, रुधिरस्य of blood, पिपासया with a thirst.
explanation: Indeed, flesh-eating creatures and very great Rakshasas followed Bharata, driven by a thirst for blood.

shloka_text: भूतग्रामाश्च बहवो मांसभक्षाः सुदारुणाः । गन्धर्वपुत्रमांसानि भोक्तुकामाः सहस्रशः ।। 7.100.23 ।।
transliteration: bhūtagrāmāśca bahavo māṃsabhakṣāḥ sudāruṇāḥ | gandharvaputramāṃsāni bhoktukāmāḥ sahasraśaḥ || 7.100.23 ||
translation: भूतग्रामाः hosts of beings, च and, बहवः many, मांसभक्षाः flesh-eaters, सुदारुणाः very terrible, गन्धर्वपुत्रमांसानि the flesh of the Gandharva princes, भोक्तुकामाः desirous of eating, सहस्रशः by thousands.
explanation: And many thousands of very terrible flesh-eating spirits, desirous of consuming the flesh of the Gandharva princes, also followed.

shloka_text: सिंहव्याघ्रवराहाणां खेचराणां च पक्षिणाम् । बहूनि वै सहस्राणि सेनाया ययुरग्रतः ।। 7.100.24 ।।
transliteration: siṃhavyāghravarāhāṇāṃ khecarāṇāṃ ca pakṣiṇām | bahūni vai sahasrāṇi senāyā yayuragrataḥ || 7.100.24 ||
translation: सिंहव्याघ्रवराहाणां of lions, tigers, and boars, खेचराणां of sky-dwellers, च and, पक्षिणाम् of birds, बहूनि many, वै indeed, सहस्राणि thousands, सेनायाः of the army, ययुः went, अग्रतः in front.
explanation: Many thousands of lions, tigers, boars, and various birds marched in front of the army.

shloka_text: अध्यर्धमासमुषिता पथि सेना निरामया । हृष्टपुष्टजनाकीर्णा केकयं समुपागमत् ।। 7.100.25 ।।
transliteration: adhyardhamāsamuṣitā pathi senā nirāmayā | hṛṣṭapuṣṭajanākīrṇā kekayaṃ samupāgamat || 7.100.25 ||
translation: अध्यर्धमासमुषिता having stayed for one and a half months, पथि on the path, सेना the army, निरामया healthy, हृष्टपुष्टजनाकीर्णा filled with joyful and well-nourished people, केकयं to Kekaya, समुपागमत् arrived.
explanation: After staying on the road for one and a half months, the army, healthy and filled with joyful and well-nourished people, arrived in Kekaya. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे शततमः सर्गः ।। 100 ।। Thus ends the hundredth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
